title: Rules the database keeps for every writer

blocks.text: The school district (invented for this practice) keeps its yearly budget plans in a `budget_plan` table (see `SCHEMA` in `guards.py`). Several scripts and a reporting tool write to that table directly, so these rules must be kept by the database itself, whoever writes:

items: A fiscal year has at most one plan with status `approved`. Any number of drafts may exist for the same year.
An approved plan can never be changed, while a draft can be edited and approved.
An approved plan can never be deleted; a draft can.

blocks.text: Write the SQL statements in `GUARDS` that keep these rules. `open_db` runs `SCHEMA` and then `GUARDS`. A refused change must raise `sqlite3.IntegrityError`. Three statements.

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE budget_plan (
    plan_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    fiscal_year INTEGER NOT NULL,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'approved')),
    amount      INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT;
"""

GUARDS = """
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_approved_per_year ON budget_plan (fiscal_year) WHERE status = 'approved';
CREATE TRIGGER approved_is_frozen BEFORE UPDATE ON budget_plan WHEN OLD.status = 'approved'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'approved plans cannot change'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER approved_is_kept BEFORE DELETE ON budget_plan WHEN OLD.status = 'approved'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'approved plans cannot be deleted'); END;
"""


def open_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", autocommit=True)
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA + GUARDS)
    return conn


if __name__ == "__main__":
    conn = open_db()
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO budget_plan VALUES ('B-1', 2028, 'approved', 4200)")
    print(conn.execute("SELECT * FROM budget_plan").fetchall())

print("delete P-1:", attempt("DELETE FROM budget_plan WHERE plan_id = 'P-1'"))
